question.leadin: This woman was the last ruler of the Ptolemaic [tall-uh-may-ik] dynasty.
question.text: Name this last queen of independent Egypt before it was conquered by the Romans.
question.clue: This ruler allegedly won a bet by drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar, and while besieged by enemies, this monarch asked for and received a basket of figs.

swap.leadin: This son of Akhenaten ruled with the assistance of the vizier Ay ("eye"), who eventually succeeded him after his death.
swap.text: Name this "Boy Pharaoh" of Egypt, whose tomb was famously discovered nearly intact by Howard Carter.
swap.clue: One of this ruler's names which invoked the god Aten was changed after his "Restoration" reversed his probable father's monotheism.

question.leadin: This structure is the burial place for the Pharaoh Khufu.
question.text: Name this limestone structure, which is the only of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
question.answerHtml: The Great Pyramid of Giza (Or Great Pyramid of Khufu, or Pyramid of Cheops , prompt on pyramid or The Pyramids )
question.clue: Slave labor was long thought to have been used to build this structure, but many archaeologists believe that thousands of skilled laborers were used instead over a 20 year period.

swap.leadin: The Greeks referred to this man as Ozymandias.
swap.text: Name this "great" Egyptian pharaoh who defeated the Nile "Sea People" and claimed a victory at the 1274 BCE Battle of Kadesh.
swap.clue: This builder of a "Sistine Chapel of Ancient Egypt" brokered a treaty with Hattusili III, and built a temple at Abu Simbel for his wife Nefertari.

question.leadin: Limestone blocks known as Talats were used in the construction of a city built by this ruler.
question.text: Name this husband of Nefertiti, a crazy pharaoh who founded a monotheistic religion venerating Aten.
question.clue: This man wrote a "Great Hymn" to his namesake and was possibly succeeded by Smenkhkare.

swap.leadin: This battle was fought along the Orontes River.
swap.text: Name this battle fought between forces divided into divisions such as Ra and Amun against Hittite forces under Muwatalli II.
swap.clue: The Amurru fought for another participant in this battle, but the newly-created Ptah division was successful in pushing them towards the Orontes River.

question.leadin: During the Byzantine period, this city was known primarily for its production of silk.
question.text: Name this Greek city in Boeotia. Its central fortress was known as the Cadmea after its mythical founder, and its army was notably led by Epaminondas.
question.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

swap.leadin: The Sherden pirates may have been one tribe of these people.
swap.text: Name this loose group who frequently attacked ancient Egypt during the collapse of the Bronze Age.
swap.clue: Egypt fought them under Merneptah and Ramses III, and they destroyed the Hittites.

question.leadin: This region's Queen Ati was depicted in an ancient relief at the Deir el-Bahri (DAYR el-BAHR-i) complex.
question.text: Name this region from which a 16th-century B.C. Egyptian expedition brought back frankincense and live myrrh trees.
question.clue: An expedition to this place led by the Chancellor Nehsi was recorded in inscriptions in the mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahri.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Ancient Egyptian agriculture.
swap.text: Irrigation canals were dug in order to control and store the water generated from this annual event. Egyptians would plant their crops in October after the end of this event.
swap.answerHtml: flooding of the Nile [or obvious equivalents indicating the overflow or inundation of the Nile River; prompt on floods]

question.leadin: The word aamu may refer to these people during their early contacts.
question.text: Name these people who invaded Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period. These people, who introduced the chariot to Egypt, constituted Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty.
question.clue: Their capital was at Avaris, and they were overthrown by Ahmose.

swap.text: Under Buyid control, the Abbasids were weakened when forced to effectively replace this senior minister with the "emir of emirs." The Ottomans later adopted a "grand" version of this title for their highest ranking official.
swap.clue: Stepping stones to this higher office held by Hemiunu included "High Steward" and "Fan-bearer on the Right Side of the King."

question.leadin: Emperor Claudius wrote a letter to the inhabitants of a city in this province about Jewish freedom of worship.
question.text: Name this region that became a Roman province a decade after its Queen Arsinoe was executed in Rome.
question.clue: Octavian ordered the death of a ruler of this region named Caesarion, whose name appeared in a "Donation."

swap.text: The existence of this pharaoh is attested to by a namesake palette that depicts him with two crowns. This pharaoh was the unifier of Upper and Lower Egypt.
swap.clue: This pharaoh who unified Upper and Lower Egypt and is depicted on a namesake palette wearing the crowns of both parts. Alternatively, name the legendary unifier of Egypt who is often identified with him.

question.text: The so-called "0 Dynasty" ends and the First Dynasty begins with Narmer unifying these two regions. The Narmer Palette found at Hierakonpolis shows him wearing the red and white crowns of these two regions.
question.answerHtml: Upper Egypt and Lower Egypt [accept Upper and Lower Egypt; accept the Sedge and the Bee]
question.clue: One of them had a name meaning "Land of the Reeds," the other was called the "Land of the North," and the two were collectively called Tawy("tah-wee").

swap.text: This Egyptian god was usually depicted as a pharaoh except for his unusual feather-decorated crown and his green skin.

question.text: The pyramid at el-Lahun, or Kahun, was designed for the second pharaoh of this name, who also built a great dike there. Except for its last female ruler Sobekneferu, the entire Twelfth Dynasty consisted only of pharaohs with this name or Amenemhat.
question.clue: This name of three Twelfth Dynasty pharaohs. Herodotus gave this name's Greek equivalent to a pharaoh who supposedly erected genitalia-topped columns to mock the cities he conquered in Asia Minor and Thrace.

swap.text: Earlier, this monarch married his sister Arsinoe III, though this notoriously incompetent monarch tried to do away with Theodotus of Aetolia, a man who nobly defend Syria but defected due to poor treatment. Still, he managed to stop Antiochus III of the Seleucids from invading at the Battle of Raphia.

question.text: Though most Egyptologists agree that ancient Egyptians were not black, they are certain that pharaohs from this dynasty were black. This last dynasty in the Third Intermediate Period lasted from 760 BC to 656 BC, and its fall marked the beginning of the Late Period.

swap.text: This man became the third head librarian of the Library around 240 BCE, and he may be best known for developing a namesake "sieve" that identifies prime numbers.
swap.clue: To accomplish one of his tasks, this man hired a number of bematists to walk 5,000 stadia.
